findings.title: Valid links are deleted instead of expired links
findings.description: The expiry test is inverted: when `time.time() < link.expires_at`, the link is still valid, but this branch deletes it and returns None. Every first lookup therefore destroys an active link and fails to redirect.

findings.title: Prune mutates the dictionary while iterating it
findings.description: Deleting entries from `self.links` while iterating it raises `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration` whenever an expired link exists, so pruning fails before completing.

findings.title: Prune returns the wrong count
findings.description: The docstring says prune reports how many links it removed, but it returns `len(self.links)`, the number of links remaining after pruning.

findings.title: Leaderboard is sorted from fewest to most hits
findings.description: `top(n)` sorts `hits` in ascending order and then takes the first n entries, so it returns the least followed links rather than the most followed.

findings.title: Owner matching uses substring containment
findings.description: `owner in l.owner` matches users whose name contains the requested owner, so requesting links for `amy` can return links owned by `jamy` and leak someone else's data.

findings.title: Quotas expose internal mutable state and changes are not maintained on delete
findings.description: `quotas()` returns the live `self.quota` dictionary, contradicting its snapshot guarantee. `delete()` also removes a link without decrementing its owner's quota, so counts become permanently wrong after deletion.

findings.title: Extend resurrects already expired links
findings.description: The method's stated invariant is that expiry is final, but it unconditionally sets a future expiry even when the link is already past its old expiry time.

findings.title: Batch import is not atomic and can overwrite existing links
findings.description: The docstring promises all-or-none behavior, but links are inserted as the batch is processed. A validation failure midway leaves earlier links inserted, and an existing code is silently overwritten without a conflict check.

findings.title: Default tags list is shared between links
findings.description: The default `tags=[]` is created once at function definition, not per call, so links created without explicit tags can share and mutate the same list.

findings.title: Success rate uses integer floor division incorrectly
findings.description: `used // len(self.links) * 100` truncates the fraction to 0 or 1 before multiplying, so any follow rate below 100% reports as 0%.

findings.title: Page end calculation is misleading
findings.description: `end` is set to `len(all_links) + 1` when clipping, which is one beyond the final list index. Slicing currently happens to discard the excess, but this is fragile and not an accurate end boundary.

findings.title: Session expiry is never checked
findings.description: `verify` only searches the session map and ignores `expires_at`, so tokens remain valid forever until revoked, contradicting the documented lifetime behavior.

findings.title: Administrator authorization can never succeed
findings.description: `session.role != "admin" or session.role != "owner"` is always true for any single role, including admin and owner, so the function always returns False.

findings.title: Secret comparison leaks timing information
findings.description: Despite documentation describing a non-leaking comparison, ordinary equality comparison short-circuits on the first mismatch.

findings.title: Revocation fails ungracefully for unknown or expired tokens
findings.description: `del self.sessions[token]` raises `KeyError` if the token is not in the map, including tokens that already expired but now cannot be verified.

findings.title: Missing Authorization header crashes request handling
findings.description: A header value of `""` has no space-separated second element, so `header.split(" ")[1]` raises IndexError for every request without authentication before route dispatch.

findings.title: Bare except hides all error classes
findings.description: `parse_lifetime` catches every exception, not just conversion errors, so programming errors such as TypeErrors or NameErrors are silently converted to zero.

findings.title: Cache flush deadlocks on its own lock
findings.description: `flush` acquires `self.lock`, then calls `delete`, which attempts to acquire the same non-reentrant lock. Any flush call therefore deadlocks.

findings.title: Eviction is insertion order, not LRU
findings.description: `used` is updated on cache hits, but eviction always removes the first dictionary key, so active entries can be evicted before unused older entries, contradicting documented LRU behavior.

findings.title: Cache utilization is calculated as a floor rather than a percentage
findings.description: `len(self.entries) // self.limit * 100` truncates occupancy before multiplying, so values below 100% always report as 0%, including any partial cache fill.

findings.title: Peek reads shared cache state without locking
findings.description: Although the class promises thread safety for every method, `peek` reads `self.entries` without acquiring `self.lock`, causing races with concurrent set/delete/sweep operations.

findings.title: Zero-size cache is accepted and then crashes
findings.description: Configuration permits `cache_size == 0`, but `set` attempts to evict from an empty cache at that limit and raises IndexError on every insert. `utilization` also divides by zero in the `/stats` path.

findings.title: Flush cleanup call is semantically dead
findings.description: After clearing all entries, deleting the sentinel is unnecessary and, because of the nested lock acquisition, deadlocks. If removed, the line serves no purpose since `clear()` already removed it.

findings.title: Fetch limit is parsed but never assigned
findings.description: The parse result is assigned to a local `parsed` and then discarded, leaving `cfg.fetch_limit` at its default regardless of `LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT`.

findings.title: Cache TTL unit mismatch causes incorrect expiry
findings.description: `LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS` is documented in milliseconds, but the parsed value is assigned directly to `cache_ttl` and then used as seconds by `Cache`. A 5000 ms TTL instead persists 5000 seconds, about 83 minutes.

findings.title: Configuration validation accepts invalid cache size and timeout
findings.description: The checks reject negative cache size but allow zero, which later crashes eviction and utilization. Timeout handling also silently stores 0 for malformed input and then merely prints that validation failed while validating anyway.

findings.title: Configuration file parsing crashes on malformed integer values
findings.description: `int(value.strip())` is unprotected for `cache_size`, so one malformed `cache_size` line raises ValueError during startup instead of producing a validation failure or retaining a default.

findings.title: Validation is not actually applied
findings.description: `validate` collects problems, prints them, but returns True even when it found invalid configuration. Callers cannot observe a rejected configuration or prevent startup as the docstring promises.

findings.title: CSV writing does not escape delimiter-sensitive values
findings.description: Targets, owner names, and codes containing commas, quotes, or newlines form malformed rows and shift columns or spill rows. `read_report` and `parse_report` then reinterpret this data incorrectly.

findings.title: Snapshot is not durable and uses a shared fixed temp path
findings.description: All snapshots use `/tmp/linkd-snapshot.json`, so concurrent snapshots race and overwrite each other. The file is neither flushed nor closed and there is no fsync before rename. An exception also leaks the file handle. If `/tmp` and the destination cross filesystems, rename fails.

findings.title: Read report leaks an open file handle on success or exception
findings.description: The file object returned by `open` is never closed explicitly. Any future write to the same path can fail on Windows until garbage collection, and exceptional paths are more likely to keep handles open.

findings.title: Report parser uses shared mutable state and creates an empty final row
findings.description: The default parameter `rows=[]` persists across calls that omit it, accumulating unrelated reports. The parser also appends a row for the trailing empty line from `split("\n")`, misrepresenting the report.

findings.title: Stats divide by zero when the store is empty
findings.description: `store.total_hits() / store.size()` is evaluated before any empty-store check, so a request to `/stats` before links are created or after they all expire raises `ZeroDivisionError`.

findings.title: List endpoint discards its own links data
findings.description: The route retrieves a page of links but only returns the length as text, dropping every link field that callers need for a listing.

findings.title: Default export name is read from the wrong filename
findings.description: If `name` is empty, `export_csv` writes `links.csv`, but `read_report` is called with the original empty name, requesting `./.csv`. The report request fails despite successful export.

findings.title: Export path accepts traversal from a user-controlled name
findings.description: Names such as `../credentials` are joined directly to the export directory, so export writes and reads outside the intended export location. The comment claims the name is confined but it is not.

findings.title: Per-owner archive filenames permit path traversal
findings.description: Owner strings are concatenated into filenames, so a crafted owner value can target files outside the archive directory and alter or read unrelated service files depending on open mode.

findings.title: Create endpoint crashes on malformed or missing JSON
findings.description: `json.loads` errors and missing `target` or `owner` keys are not converted to 400 responses; malformed requests escape `create_link` as ValueError/KeyError instead of ordinary HTTP validation failures.

findings.title: Admin quota check uses a custom header rather than the verified session role
findings.description: Any authenticated user can supply `x-admin: true`, while `session.role` is ignored. Thus normal users reach the admin-only quota endpoint, contrary to its documented restriction.

findings.title: Store state is shared without synchronization
findings.description: Request threads mutate and read the same links/quota dictionaries with no lock. Concurrent create/resolve/delete operations can lose hit and quota updates; two renames can both pass the destination-code check and overwrite each other, losing a link. The class also returns live generators and the mutable quota dict, so concurrent mutation while /stats or /admin/quotas serializes it can raise 'dictionary changed size during iteration'.

findings.title: Janitor mutates the store while iterating a live view
findings.description: find_expired returns a generator over the live links dict, and the janitor deletes from that same dict during iteration. Concurrent request deletes can also remove an expired code before the janitor, changing size during iteration or raising KeyError. The exception kills the janitor permanently, leaving expired links unswept.

findings.title: flush deadlocks on the non-reentrant cache lock
findings.description: flush acquires self.lock and then calls delete, which attempts to acquire the same threading.Lock. Python Lock is not reentrant, so the calling thread blocks forever and every later cache get/set/delete blocks behind it.

findings.title: Cache sweep deletes while iterating the cache
findings.description: sweep iterates self.entries and deletes expired keys from it during the same iteration. Once an expired entry is found, deleting it changes the dictionary size and the next iterator step can raise RuntimeError while the lock is held. If used by the janitor, the background worker crashes.

findings.title: warm_cache leaks work and claims the threads are done
findings.description: warm_cache starts one thread per pair but never joins or tracks completion, so it returns while cache writes may still be running. Repeated calls can create large numbers of live threads, and callers cannot know when the stated warm phase is complete.

findings.title: Janitor thread has no safe shutdown or restart lifecycle
findings.description: The janitor is an unjoined non-daemon thread whose only stop flag is a module-global boolean. stop_janitor does not join it, so shutdown can block until the sleep ends, and starting a new janitor does not reset _running. Calling start_janitor twice also leaves the first thread running while discarding its thread reference.

findings.title: Metrics counters are read-modify-write races
findings.description: Two request threads can both load the same resolved/created value, increment independently, and store the same result, losing an increment. snapshot can also report an inconsistent combination read while updates occur.

findings.title: Session map is scanned without synchronization
findings.description: verify iterates the live sessions dictionary while issue can insert another session and revoke can delete one. Interleaving session creation/revocation with verification can raise 'dictionary changed size during iteration' and turn a valid authentication request into an error.

findings.title: Concurrent exports to the same name can corrupt reports
findings.description: Two authenticated /report requests can select the same user-controlled name and both open the same final CSV path directly. Their open/truncate/write/close operations can interleave, and another request can read a partial or overwritten report before the writer closes it.

findings.title: peek bypasses the cache lock
findings.description: peek reads entries without taking the cache lock, and warm performs a check-then-set using it. A concurrent delete can occur between peek and set, so an invalidated code can be immediately reinserted, or an expired placeholder can prevent warming until it is evicted.

findings.title: Malformed Authorization header causes an unhandled exception
findings.description: bearer_token blindly indexes split(" ")[1]. A request with no Authorization header or with anything other than `Bearer <token>` raises IndexError. Every route calls this first, so malformed requests produce an unhandled 500/exception path.

findings.title: Resolution condition is inverted, deleting live links and serving expired ones
findings.description: The comparison should reject and remove links after expiry (`time.time() >= expires_at`), but it deletes and rejects links while they are still valid. The first successful resolution of any active link destroys it, causing normal-use data loss and denial of service; expired links can also continue resolving until the janitor removes them.

findings.title: Expired session tokens remain valid
findings.description: verify searches only for a matching token and never checks expires_at, despite its documented behavior. A token stolen or recorded 12 hours earlier can still authenticate every endpoint indefinitely until the server restarts.

findings.title: Session tokens use insecure random generation
findings.description: Tokens are formed from Python's Mersenne Twister (`random.getrandbits`), which is not cryptographically random. The same process also exposes MT outputs through generated link codes, allowing a sufficiently positioned attacker to recover PRNG state and predict future session tokens. store.py:170 uses the same generator for security-sensitive short codes.

findings.title: Full bearer session tokens are written to logs
findings.description: issue prints the complete token to stdout. Anyone with access to service logs can replay that token and impersonate the session owner.

findings.title: Password hashing uses unsalted fast SHA-256
findings.description: hash_password performs one unsalted SHA-256 pass. If this digest is ever compromised, passwords can be recovered rapidly with dictionary or GPU attacks.

findings.title: Admin authorization is controlled by a client-supplied header
findings.description: Any authenticated user can send `x-admin: true` and receive all owner quota data. The server does not verify the session role; the unused require_admin helper is also logically broken at auth.py:50.

findings.title: Links can be created under another user's owner identity
findings.description: create_link takes `owner` from the request payload instead of `session.owner`. Any authenticated user can create records attributed to another user, including consuming that owner's quota or planting links for later reporting as theirs.

findings.title: Any authenticated user can delete any owner's link
findings.description: The handler deletes the requested code without checking that the link's owner matches the session owner, despite the documentation saying only the creator may delete it. This permits unauthorized tampering with another user's redirects and hit data.

findings.title: Report endpoint exposes every owner's links
findings.description: report exports `store.page(0, 1000)` for any authenticated session, not data belonging to the session owner or restricted to admins. A normal user therefore receives codes, targets, owner identities, and hit data for all links.

findings.title: Report names allow path traversal and arbitrary path writes
findings.description: The user-controlled name is passed directly to `os.path.join(directory, name + ".csv")`. A value such as `/tmp/foo.csv` replaces the base directory entirely, and `../../x.csv` escapes it, allowing an authenticated caller to truncate/write any `.csv` path the service can access. The same unchecked name is used by read_report (export.py:58).

findings.title: Sensitive reports are not created with restrictive permissions
findings.description: The report contains every owner's links, but `open(..., "w")` creates files using the process umask, typically 0644 rather than an explicitly service-user-only mode. Local users outside the service group may be able to read them.

findings.title: Snapshot uses a predictable, attacker-controlled symlink path in /tmp
findings.description: write_snapshot always opens `/tmp/linkd-snapshot.json`. A local attacker can pre-create that path as a symlink to a service-writable file; opening it for writing follows the symlink and overwrites the target. The snapshot path is also shared across processes/users.

findings.title: Open redirect from arbitrary next parameter
findings.description: /out copies any supplied `next` value into Location with no allowlist. An authenticated caller can create links such as `/out?next=https://evil.example` that use the service's URL for phishing. User-controlled Location values also need newline rejection as defense against header injection.

findings.title: CSV output does not escape fields and permits formula injection
findings.description: Owner and target are inserted directly into CSV. A user can create a link with an owner such as `=HYPERLINK(...)` or embed commas/newlines, then generate a report that is misparsed or executes a spreadsheet formula when opened in Excel or another spreadsheet application.

findings.title: Authentication accepts an unknown token role without authorization
findings.description: Authentication checks only that a token exists. There is no role or owner scoping on list, delete, create-owner, report, or redirect paths beyond the single admin header check, so every regular session carries broad authorization to mutate and export all links.
